title: Reacting
note: Maya: one recording of 26 lines in script order → s00 … s25. Daniel: 18 questions → q01 … q18. {curly} marks the phrase inside an answer.

intro.t: Hi again. Before you answer, show the examiner how you feel. A quick reaction organises your answer, and buys you a second or two. Two for things you love, two for things you don't, and two longer ones that sound really fluent.

close.t: Great work. Tomorrow, try them on your own life. What do you love, and what's not really your thing?

reels.note: Say it with a smile. The 'Oh' is what makes it sound real.

ex.t: {Oh, I love} cooking! My grandmother taught me, and now I make pancakes every Sunday.

ex.q: Do you enjoy going to the beach?
ex.t: {Oh, I love} the beach, especially early in the morning, when it's quiet.

ex.q: Do you like going to concerts?
ex.t: {Oh, I love} concerts! There's nothing like singing along with thousands of people.

reels.note: Followed by a noun or an -ing word: a huge fan of jazz, of reading, of puzzle games.

ex.q: What kind of music do you listen to?
ex.t: {I'm a huge fan of} pop, but lately I've been listening to a lot of jazz too.

ex.q: Do you play any video games?
ex.t: Yes, {I'm a huge fan of} puzzle games, because they make me think.
{I'm a huge fan of} fantasy novels. I can read one in a weekend.

reels.note: The missing piece for a teenager who dislikes the topic. Then add what you DO like.

ex.t: {I'm not really into} shopping. I'd rather buy things online and save time.
{I'm not really into} football, but I always watch the World Cup with my family.
{I'm not really into} dancing. I usually end up chatting at the side!

reels.note: Sounds calm, never rude. Always give a reason straight after.

ex.t: {It's not really my thing.} I like a proper bed too much.

ex.q: Would you like to try a winter sport?
ex.t: {It's not really my thing.} I hate being cold, so I'd rather try surfing.

ex.q: Do you enjoy going to museums?
ex.t: {It's not really my thing,} unless there's something interactive to do.

reels.note: Organises your answer AND counts as a complex structure: examiners notice it.

ex.q: What's the best thing about your school?
ex.t: {What I love about} my school {is} that the teachers really listen to us.

ex.q: Do you like the area where you live?
ex.t: Yes! {What I love about} my area {is} that everything is within walking distance.
{What I love about} weekends {is} that nobody tells me what time to get up.

reels.bt: What I love about it is…

reels.p: If there's one thing I …, it's …
reels.note: Works for love AND hate: one thing I can't stand, one thing I look forward to.

ex.q: Is there any food you don't like?
ex.t: {If there's one thing I} can't stand, {it's} mushrooms. I just don't like the texture.

ex.q: What do you enjoy most about holidays?
ex.t: {If there's one thing I} look forward to, {it's} sleeping late!

ex.q: What do you find difficult about learning English?
ex.t: {If there's one thing I} find hard, {it's} phrasal verbs. There are so many of them!

reels.bt: If there's one thing I love, it's…
